# Results — Study 503 (Expected Idiosyncratic Skewness): does the skewed tail underperform?

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The Boyer-Mitton-Vorkink (2010)
**expected idiosyncratic skewness** sort — each month, regress every name's daily returns on the
market over the trailing 12 months, take the **skewness of the residuals** (the own-name,
market-orthogonal tail), form quintiles, and go **long the low-skew names, short the high-skew
(lottery) names** — tested on a **transparent large-cap proxy**. True expected idio-skew is a
CRSP-universe (thousands of names, small-caps included) object; yfinance gives only a large-cap
slice, so we run the sort on a fixed **S&P-100-style basket** and call it a proxy throughout.
Offline core + synthetic control are deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce
every number.*

## The verdict, earned — Signal `NONE` · Tradability `MIRAGE` · "Skewed losers?" `BUSTED`

Skewness-preference says investors over-pay for a fat idiosyncratic right tail, so the
positively-skewed names should **underperform**. On this large-cap survivor proxy the effect is
simply **absent**: the low-skew quintile (Q1) returned **+15.6%/yr** and the high-skew quintile
(Q5) **+16.6%/yr**, so the textbook long-low / short-high book earns a gross **−1.0%/yr** at HAC
**t = −0.41** — a coin, slightly on the wrong side, placebo *p* = 0.66. The spread stays near
zero across tertile / quintile / decile cuts and in both halves of the sample; it never clears
*t* = 2 *gross* in either direction. The published CRSP cross-sectional anomaly lives in small,
low-priced, retail-held names; on liquid, surviving large-caps the residual-skew sort carries no
forward information. `NONE` on Signal (the claimed low-skew edge is absent, and it is
**survivorship**-tilted — named on the axis), `MIRAGE` on Tradability (no positive gross edge;
costs merely turn a near-zero spread into a *losing* one), and `BUSTED` on the folklore (the
skewed tail had the *highest* quintile return).

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted closes — a fixed **S&P-100-style 79-name large-cap basket + SPY** (public, no key) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**5,385** trading days; **21.4** years; partial 2026-06 bar dropped) |
| As-of | **2026-05-31** (last complete month-end); inputs fingerprint `abdf2637ac09` |
| Signal | **idio-skew** = skewness of the residual from a trailing-12-month daily market (SPY) regression, per name, at month-end |
| Sort | rank cross-section by idio-skew → quintiles Q1 (low) … Q5 (high); equal-weight next-month return |
| Trade | long Q1 (low-skew) / short Q5 (high-skew), monthly; monthly signal ⇒ full monthly turnover |
| Costs | 20 bps one-way per leg × turnover + 50 bps/yr short borrow on the high-skew leg |

> **Proxy + survivorship caveat (named on the Signal axis).** A fixed ~79-name surviving
> large-cap basket is the *least* lottery-prone slice of the market — the opposite end from the
> small, low-priced, retail-held names where Boyer-Mitton-Vorkink find the skewness-preference
> premium. On survivors, a positively-skewed residual often flags a high-beta growth name that
> went on to lead the bull market, not an over-priced lottery ticket, so the sort carries little
> of the original signal. The bias points *against* the anomaly here, and we say so: this tape
> can show the published effect **does not survive** the large-cap, survivor universe — it
> cannot certify the CRSP result either way. **Opt-in guard:** widen to a few-thousand-name
> micro-cap panel (paid feed) to test the effect in its native habitat.

## The cross-section — flat, with the skewed tail mildly *ahead*

251 monthly cross-sections (2005-06 → 2026-04). Each quintile's next-month return,
equal-weighted, annualised:

| quintile | idio-skew rank | mean / yr | vol | Sharpe |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Q1 | **lowest** skew (symmetric) | +15.6% | 15.1% | **1.03** |
| Q2 | | +12.4% | 14.3% | 0.86 |
| Q3 | | +14.8% | 15.5% | 0.96 |
| Q4 | | +16.1% | 18.1% | 0.89 |
| Q5 | **highest** skew (lottery) | **+16.6%** | 17.5% | 0.95 |

The skewness story predicts Q1 ≫ Q5. Here the line is essentially **flat** and tilts the *wrong*
way on return: the high-skew tail (Q5, +16.6%/yr) edges out the low-skew tail (Q1, +15.6%/yr).
Q1 keeps the best Sharpe (lower vol), but that is a low-vol artefact, not a skewness penalty on
Q5.

## The trade — long low-skew / short high-skew is a coin gross, a loser net

| book | mean / yr | Sharpe | HAC *t* | win-rate | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Q1 − Q5 (long low-skew, short high-skew), **gross** | **−1.0%** | −0.09 | **−0.41** | 45% | 0.659 |
| Q1 − Q5, **net** (20 bps/leg + 50 bps/yr borrow) | −6.3% | −0.57 | **−2.54** | 41% | — |

Gross, the textbook trade is **indistinguishable from zero** (HAC *t* = −0.41, placebo
*p* = 0.66, a sub-coin 45% win-rate) — the claimed low-skew edge is simply not there. The *net*
book is significantly negative (*t* = −2.54), but that significance is a **cost artefact**: a
high-turnover monthly long-short that earns ~0 gross is dragged below zero by 2 × 20 bps/leg plus
borrow. There is no positive gross edge for costs to erode — the negative net *t* certifies the
*frictions*, not a tradable skewness anomaly. `REAL` requires *t* ≥ 2 **gross, in the claimed
direction**; this is *t* = −0.41.

## Robustness — flat everywhere, never significant gross

| cut | n | mean / yr (low − high) | HAC *t* | win-rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| tertiles (Q1 − Q3) | 251 | −1.8% | −0.86 | 45% |
| **quintiles (Q1 − Q5)** | 251 | **−1.0%** | **−0.41** | 45% |
| deciles (Q1 − Q10) | 251 | −3.7% | −1.14 | 45% |

Cutting harder into the tails leaves the spread small and insignificant (deciles reach only
*t* = −1.14) — no edge emerges in either direction as the cut sharpens.

| sub-period | n | mean / yr | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2005–2015 | 127 | −0.6% | −0.17 |
| 2016–2026 | 124 | −1.5% | −0.42 |

Near zero in **both** halves — not a regime that hides a flipped sign, just no signal.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful (and seed-robust)

A deterministic monthly panel with a **planted skewness penalty** (high-skew names made to
underperform next month by ``edge`` × standardised idio-skew) confirms the sort + inference
recover a *real* low-minus-high edge when one is present, and find **nothing** when it is absent.
Per the house bar, the control's *t* is averaged over **20 seeds**:

| planted edge | Q1 − Q5 mean / yr | HAC *t* (seed 503) | seed-robust mean *t* (20 seeds) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.000** (no edge) | −0.5% | −0.30 | **+0.24** (sd 1.08) |
| **+0.004** (real skew penalty) | +12.9% | +8.12 | **+8.58** (sd 1.28) |

With **no** planted edge the harness sits near *t* = 0 across seeds (no false positive); with a
modest planted penalty it turns the spread cleanly positive at mean *t* = +8.58 over 20 seeds.
So the machinery is honest: the **flat** *t* on the real tape is a genuine feature of the
large-cap survivor cross-section, not a coding artefact, and a *real* skewness-preference effect
would have shown up as a clean **positive** spread had one existed here.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The claimed low-skew outperformance is **absent** on this tape; the gross
  long-low / short-high spread is **−1.0%/yr at HAC *t* = −0.41** (placebo *p* = 0.66) — a coin,
  if anything on the wrong side. The result is flat across cut granularity and both sub-periods,
  and the universe is a **survivorship**-tilted large-cap proxy (named on the Signal axis). The
  published CRSP cross-sectional anomaly is not reproduced — and cannot be certified — on a
  surviving large-cap universe.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is no positive gross edge; the only statistically significant
  number (net *t* = −2.54) is a **cost artefact** on a near-zero gross spread, not a deployable
  skewness short. Nothing here to allocate to.
- **"Skewed losers"? — BUSTED.** On liquid, surviving large-caps the positively-skewed tail did
  **not** underperform — Q5 posted the **highest** quintile return (+16.6%/yr vs Q1's +15.6%).
  The skewness-preference morality tale is a small-cap / retail-lottery phenomenon that does not
  generalise to the names most large-cap investors actually hold.
